title: northstar-insurance-llm-pilot-scratchpad
content:
Notes to self: quick reconnaissance for NorthStar Insurance (regional insurer, mid-market P&C + small commercial). Heard via broker meetup that they piloted a claims triage chatbot internally (pilot stalled Q4). Good candidate for an inference-cost/latency play: high call volumes, strict SLA windows for triage, and legacy on-prem LLM experiments that failed economics test.

Key account summary:
- HQ: Minneapolis; ~900 employees; $1.2B GA revenue (est)
- Tech stack: Azure tenancy (multi-sub), internal data lake on Snowflake, legacy on-prem NLP model for NLG (reports suggest high infra ops burden)
- Existing vendors: Claims workflow vendor (VerityClaims), contact center (FiveReflect? verify), IT outsourcing partner (regional MSP)

Primary stakeholders (map for outreach):
- VP Digital Ops: Elaine Montoya — owns CX+automation initiatives, pushes pilot approvals; good exec sponsor target
- Head of Claims Innovation: Marcus Bell — technical buyer; curious about latency/throughput and eval metrics (peak claims after storms)
- Director of Security & Compliance: Asha Ramesh — gating factor for private deployment, KMS/HSM requirements
- SRE/Platform lead: Samir Patel — will care about deployment model, VPC peering, telemetry hooks

Hypothesis (what they care about):
- Cut per-claim triage cost by 30–50% while keeping time-to-resolution SLOs
- Maintain PII control (HIPAA-esque regs? probably state regs + PII for claimants) — leans toward Redwood Private or Dedicated with strict audit logs
- Ease of ops: prefer a single vendor that can support both hosted API for quick POC and private for production rollover

Quick win pilot idea (3-week sandbox):
1) Week 0: ingest sample anonymized claim transcripts (we ask for 500 rows) + canonical triage questions
2) Week 1: zero-friction hosted PoC using Redwood API (low-friction, rapid results) — measure latency, token cost, and accuracy vs. current rule-based triage
3) Week 2: demo to stakeholders with cost/latency dashboard + transcript comparisons; propose Dedicated/Private runway if accuracy and economics line up
Metrics to track:
- Median generation latency (end-to-end) 95th pctl
- Per-claim token cost (compare to current cost baseline)
- Triage accuracy (human-labeled 200-sample set)
- Fallback rate to human operator

Outbound email draft (short) — first touch (cold but warm):
Subject: Pilot idea to cut claims triage overhead at NorthStar
Hi Elaine —
We help insurance teams run LLMs for customer triage and claims workflows with predictable latency and cost. I saw NorthStar ran a claims chatbot pilot last year — curious if you’re open to a 3-week sandbox where we show actual latency/cost comparisons vs. your current setup (no heavy infra lift).
Quick call next week?
— Maya (Redwood Inference)

Follow-up / Value prop bullets (for LinkedIn/InMail):
- 15–50% cost improvement vs on-prem experiments via smart batching + KV caching
- SLA-backed Dedicated capacity for predictable peak storm volumes
- Private deployment option with KMS + audit logging for sensitive PII workflows

Discovery questions to surface during call:
- What was the primary reason the prior pilot didn’t move forward? (ops cost? accuracy? security?)
- Typical claims volume (avg/day) and peak day multiplier (storm/seasonal)?
- Do you have a sanitized dataset we can run a 500-sample quick scan on?
- Which vendor currently handles triage routing and what integration points exist?
- What are your must-have compliance controls (data residency, retention, encryption)?

Objection handling quick cheatsheet:
- "We already have an on-prem model": acknowledge investment, then lean into measured cost comparison + hybrid path (hosted PoC -> Dedicated/private migration). Offer to replicate a 2-week cost model for their recent experiment so we can show delta.
- "Security/compliance concerns": highlight private deployments, KMS/HSM options, audit logs, SOC2 mention (we should add exact spec later), and proposed red-team review window during pilot.
- "Ops burden / we don't have bandwidth": propose a concierge pilot: Redwood handles ingestion, prompt engineering, metric dashboarding for the sandbox; we aim to hand off a proven blueprint post-proof.

Meeting agenda (30 min initial intro):
- 5m intros & objective alignment (what success looks like)
- 10m quick tech + ops Qs (data flow, integrations, compliance)
- 10m demo of similar insurance pilot (screenshots + cost dashboard)
- 5m next steps / ask for sample data / decision timeline

Internal TODOs (for me):
- [ ] Pull sample deck from previous insurance pilot (ask Jonah for slide pack)
- [ ] Build 1-page cost-comparison template (Priya to help w/ cost model)
- [ ] Draft DTS/POC data transfer agreement template for legal (put on Confluence and ping Asha in security)
- [ ] Create short demo video clip (1–2 min) showing latency dashboard and fallback logs

Notes / conversation fragments to keep: (copy-paste style)
- Marcus prefers numbers: "Show me 95th percentile latency under 300ms for triage path"
- Elaine cares about org adoption: "If it reduces human review by X%, we can justify headcount reallocation"
- Samir will ask about VPC peering and Prometheus metrics endpoint — prep standard SRE runbook snippet

Risks / unknowns:
- They may require EU residency for certain PII (unlikely but verify via legal).
- Prior vendor lock-in with claims system may make integration slow — need API contract early.

Next scheduled actions:
- Wed 2025-02-12: Jonah intro to Marcus (internal warm intro attempt)
- Fri 2025-02-14: send first touch email to Elaine (personalize with ref to broker meetup notes)

Quick link stash (for outreach kit):
- Redwood insurance case study (internal): confluence link above
- Demo dashboard gif (assets/internal/demos/claims-dashboard.gif)

Random scratch ideas (brain dump):
- Could offer a short "storm-mode" test where we simulate 10x peak load to show autoscaling and Dedicated SLA behavior
- Consider offering a small pilot discount if they commit to a 6-month Dedicated runway (sales to discuss)

End notes: keep language simple for Execs; come loaded with numbers for Marcus. Avoid heavy ML jargon in initial outreach.
